title: Best payment gateway for WooCommerce: UAE providers compared
summary: Read on to discover 7 payment gateways for WooCommerce and compare them based on fees, WooCommerce setup, available features, and payout speed.
body_markdown:
You’ve decided to sell through WooCommerce. Your products are good to go, your store is ready to launch – but there’s just one more decision to make before your customers can place an order: which payment gateway will power your checkout?


That choice affects how quickly you can get your checkout live, which payment methods you can offer customers, what it costs you to process each order, when the money lands in your bank account, and how smoothly customers move through the checkout process.


There are a number of providers to choose from in the UAE, each with slightly different features and fees.


You’ll need to check things like:


- Which payment methods are available through the WooCommerce integration


- Which currencies customers can use and which currency reaches your account


- How quickly you can access the money from each order


- If you can embed the checkout into your own product


- Whether the provider offers other payment tools if you eventually start selling beyond your online store


So, let’s compare seven WooCommerce payment gateway providers available to UAE businesses and go over everything you should check before choosing one.


In this article:


- WooCommerce payment gateways in the UAE compared


- What to look for in a WooCommerce payment gateway in the UAE


- Ziina: Get your WooCommerce checkout live quickly


- Stripe

- Amazon Payment Services


Launching a WooCommerce store in the UAE? Connect Ziina to your checkout, start accepting payments, and manage all your sales through one payment platform.

## What to look for in a WooCommerce payment gateway in the UAE


Finding a payment gateway provider that works with WooCommerce is the easy part.


Figuring out which one works for your specific store setup and day-to-day operations in the UAE takes a bit more research.


Let’s start with one of the biggest non-negotiables.


### Make sure the plugin fits your actual WooCommerce setup


Ready-made WooCommerce payment plugins give you a clear setup process, but they still have to work alongside the WordPress version, WooCommerce version, theme, and extensions your store already uses.


That combination can change as different parts of your store are updated.


[WooCommerce recommends](https://woocommerce.com/document/how-to-update-woocommerce/) keeping WordPress, WooCommerce, themes, extensions, and payment gateways current while testing important updates before applying them to a live store.


Take an even closer look at the plugin’s compatibility if you need subscription support, memberships, saved payment methods, custom checkout fields, or a theme that changes the standard checkout flow. For example, WooCommerce documents


[payment-gateway support for subscriptions](https://woocommerce.com/document/subscriptions/payment-gateways/) separately because the available subscription features can depend on the specific gateway extension.


Before choosing a provider, check:


- Which WooCommerce and WordPress versions the plugin supports


- Whether it supports Checkout Blocks and the other checkout features or extensions your store uses


- Whether the features you need are available to UAE merchants specifically


- When the plugin was last updated


- Who handles support if the gateway conflicts with another part of your store


### Calculate what each payment costs and how payout speed affects the total


The first transaction rate or monthly fee you see might not tell you what it really costs to process payments.


The real cost of your WooCommerce payment gateway could include:


- A percentage of each transaction


- A fixed fee per payment


- International card charges or extra fees based on currency conversion rates


- Setup or monthly account fees


- Refund or dispute fees


- Faster-payout fees


To compare different providers’ pricing, run the numbers using a typical order for your store.


If your average order is AED 150, calculate what you’ll pay for a domestic AED order and how much more an international order could cost.


Then look at when the remaining money becomes available – and whether accessing it sooner costs extra.


Check:


- How long settlement usually takes


- How often payouts are sent


- Whether weekends or UAE public holidays can slow things down


- Whether new accounts start with longer payout timelines


- Whether faster payout or cashout options are available, what they cost, and who qualifies


### Confirm which payment methods and currencies are available through WooCommerce


Providers don’t always offer the same features across every platform, so you’ll want to double check what’s available through the provider’s WooCommerce integration specifically.


Confirm which payment methods will appear at checkout and whether you actually need them. Depending on your customers, you might want to offer alternative payment methods alongside standard card payments:


- Major credit and debit cards


- Apple Pay and Google Pay


- International cards


- PayPal – check if this is available through your chosen gateway or requires a separate WooCommerce integration


- UAE Buy Now Pay Later (BNPL) options like Tabby and Tamara


- Offline payment options, such as cash on delivery or check payments


If you sell to customers outside the UAE, also check:


- Which currencies customers can use at checkout


- Which currency you receive when the payment is settled


- BNPL options for shoppers abroad, like Afterpay and Klarna (if you need it for your use case)


Now that you know what to compare, let’s take a closer look at each provider.

## Stripe


Stripe is a global payment infrastructure platform used across websites, apps, subscriptions, marketplaces, and custom payment flows.


Stripe’s WooCommerce plugin extension supports Checkout Blocks, saved payment methods, and WooCommerce Subscriptions.¹


Stripe’s UAE rate starts at 2.9% + AED 1 for domestic cards, with an additional 1% for international cards and another 1% when currency conversion is required.² Eligible businesses can pay an additional fee for Instant Payouts, while standard payout timing depends on the account.²


Could be a fit if:


Your store uses more advanced WooCommerce features like subscriptions, saved payment methods, or Checkout Blocks, and you want an official plugin maintained by Stripe and WooCommerce.


## Mamo


Mamo is a UAE-based business finance platform. Alongside its WooCommerce integration, it offers tools for collecting customer payments and managing how your business spends and sends money.³


On the payment collection side, Mamo offers payment links, invoices, subscriptions, and APIs. Corporate cards, expense controls, approval workflows, and supplier payouts extend the platform into company spending.³


Pricing depends on which of Mamo’s two standard plans you choose:


- The Growth plan has no monthly fee and charges 2.9% + AED 1 for UAE cards.


- The Premium plan costs AED 99 per month and is positioned for businesses collecting at least AED 50,000 monthly, with a lower UAE-card rate of 2.7% + AED 0.80.⁴


Premium also lowers the published rates for international cards, non-AED payments, and same-day settlement. Both plans list a standard settlement period of five business days, with faster three-day payouts available subject to an early access fee – and same-day settlement when payments are received before 3pm GST.⁴


Could be a fit if:


You want a UAE-based provider that combines WooCommerce payment collection with corporate cards and spend-management tools.


## Telr


[Telr](https://ziina.com/blog/telr-payment-gateway) is a UAE-based payment gateway provider for accepting payments through websites, mobile apps, and other online channels.


Its WooCommerce extension supports a Telr-hosted payment page that returns customers to your store after payment. It also includes a Seamless Payment Mode, which can be toggled on through the Telr settings within the WooCommerce dashboard.⁶


The extension has been tested with WooCommerce version 8. Telr also lists WordPress, PHP, and cURL requirements, so check those against your current store before installing it.⁶


Telr structures its UAE pricing around monthly payment volume. Its Entry, Small, and Medium plans each combine a monthly charge with a different transaction rate.⁷


This means your expected sales volume is an important part of the pricing comparison.


Alongside its WooCommerce extension, Telr’s payment-gateway offering includes hosted checkout, iframe integration, direct APIs, and mobile SDKs for websites and apps.⁸ Its UAE plans also include access to local support.⁷


Could be a fit if:


You want a regional provider with both hosted and seamless WooCommerce checkout options and prefer a pricing plan based on monthly sales volume.


## PayTabs


PayTabs is a regional payment provider with a ready-made WooCommerce plugin that can be installed through the WordPress admin panel or uploaded manually using File Transfer Protocol.⁹


PayTabs says the plugin can be installed and activated without a technical background, although you’ll still need to connect it to your PayTabs account and configure the relevant settings.⁹


The PayTabs WooCommerce plugin supports major credit cards, digital wallets, and regional BNPL options in the UAE, depending on the features enabled for your merchant profile.¹⁸


Outside the WooCommerce integration, PayTabs offers payment links, digital invoicing, QR payments, repeat billing, APIs, mobile SDKs, and plugins for other eCommerce platforms.¹¹,¹²


PayTabs doesn’t publish one standard UAE payment-gateway rate on its public pricing page. Ask the company to confirm the full fee structure, settlement schedule, and WooCommerce payment methods included in your account before signing up.¹⁰


Could be a fit if:


You want a regional provider with a ready-made WooCommerce plugin and access to a wider range of MENA payment methods and integrations.


## Network International


Network International is a long-established regional payment provider with a dedicated WooCommerce plugin for its N-Genius Online gateway.¹³


The plugin is free to download and designed to connect a WooCommerce store to N-Genius Online without a custom build. The cards, wallets, and local payment methods available depend on the merchant account.¹³


Transactions can be managed through the N-Genius portal, including refunds, reconciliation, reports, and other payment activity.¹³


Network International also offers hosted payment pages, Pay By Link, virtual terminal payments, direct APIs, web and mobile SDKs, fraud-management tools, and plugins for other eCommerce platforms. It has operations across the Middle East and Africa, with support available 24/7.¹⁴


You’ll need to confirm pricing and settlement terms with Network International – along with exactly how the WooCommerce plugin will work for your store, the payment methods and currencies included, processing rates, settlement timing, and support arrangements.¹⁴


Could be a fit if:


You want a long-established regional acquiring provider with a WooCommerce plugin, merchant portal, and wider set of online payment tools.


## Amazon Payment Services


Amazon Payment Services is a MENA-focused payment-services provider with an official WooCommerce plugin and two main checkout routes.¹⁵


The hosted route sends customers to an Amazon Payment Services payment page before returning them to your store. The custom route gives you more control over the payment flow but requires additional configuration.¹⁵


The plugin supports major cards, Apple Pay, saved cards through tokenization, refunds through the WooCommerce order screen, multi-currency configuration, sandbox testing, and Tabby for eligible UAE and Saudi Arabian accounts.¹⁵


Amazon Payment Services also offers Payment Links, APIs, installments, Buy Now, Pay Later options in eligible markets, and plugins for other eCommerce platforms.¹⁵ ¹⁶ ¹⁷


Could be a fit if:


You want a MENA-focused provider with hosted and custom WooCommerce checkout routes, sandbox testing, and support for cards, Apple Pay, installments, and eligible regional payment methods.
